newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: TENNIS-HINGIS IN SECOND FINAL IN A WEEK.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS IN SECOND FINAL IN A WEEK.

text.p: Swiss teenager Martina Hingis reached her second final in seven days with a 3-6 6-2 7-6 win over Germany's Anke Huber at the European indoor championship on Saturday.
The semifinal was a rematch of last week's final in Filderstadt where Hingis recorded her first career tournament success.
Hingis will meet the Czech Republic's Jana Novotna in Sunday's final here.
Novotna, the fourth seed, reached her third final of the season after outlasting second seed and defending champion Iva Majoli 5-7 6-2 6-2 in two hours 12 minutes.
Hingis looked poised to secure her place in the final when she broke Huber to go 5-4 up in the third set. But the feisty German immediately broke back and held serve to force a tie-break.
With the sell-out crowd urging her on, Hingis quickly re-grouped and took control of the tie-break 6-1, but once again Huber stormed back, saving five match points to reach 6-6 and silence the crowd.
However, the German was unable to sustain the comeback as Hingis took the next two points and the match.
"With five match points I thought there was no way I was going to lose," said Hingis, the fifth seed and world number nine. "When it was 6-6 I got a little nervous.
"I thought to myself, if I lose this point I'm going to break my racket into little pieces."

Not only was Hingis' immense talent on display during her match but so was the 16 year-old's temperament, particularly during a tense third set when she slammed her racket on to the court six times, receiving a warning for abuse.
"When I throw my racket it helps me concentrate," excplained Hingis.
In the other semifinal, Majoli and Novotna battled over the first set for 65 minutes and although Novotna was fighting off a a bad cold it was Majoli who appeared drained by the effort.
In the second and third sets Novotna recorded early breaks, jumping out to 3-1 leads, and never allowed the 19 year-old Croat back into the match.
"I was very sick today with a cold," said Novotna, who will be looking for her 12th career title. "But I just wanted to win so much.
"I was so disappointed, so tired after the first with the way I was feeling I wasn't sure I would last.
"But after the first set I started to relax and played so much better. It was a completely different game."
